made_by: orchestrator's diagnosis (Opus), written into the file by the builder (Claude Sonnet 5.5)
basis: output/remediation/calibration/releases-evidence/fact_checker-gold-diagnosis.md, sections (1) and (3), on the draw of calibrations teaser-2026-10-09b and -09c (same seed, same cases). The scoring key of a case is run/stage/site_id.

checker_fails.name: Westbury Camp
checker_fails.card: On a slope of the Mendip Hills, Westbury Camp is an Iron Age hill fort whose narrow bank may once have carried a dry stone wall, its north east defences largely destroyed by small quarries.
checker_fails.label: hair-split
checker_fails.note: 'narrow bank' against 'narrow top of the bank'

checker_fails.name: Al-Rabadha
checker_fails.card: On the pilgrim route from Kufa to Mecca, Al-Rabadha is dominated by a palace of 13 rooms opening on a central courtyard, where ovens, grain storage and a glass-making furnace were found.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Broch of Mousa
checker_fails.card: On the island of Mousa in Shetland rises the Broch of Mousa, the tallest broch still standing, thought to have been built circa 300 BC and besieged by Earl Harald Maddadsson in 1153.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Pilgrims' Way
checker_fails.card: The Pilgrims' Way, supposedly walked from Winchester to Becket's shrine at Canterbury, follows an ancient trackway on the North Downs, dated by finds to 600–450 BC and probably older.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Kit's Coty House
checker_fails.card: Near Aylesford in Kent, three stones still carry the capstone of Kit's Coty House, a long barrow built circa 4000 BCE, its mound ploughed flat yet traced in aerial photographs.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Carwynnen Quoit
checker_fails.card: Also known as the Giant's Frying Pan, Carwynnen Quoit is a portal dolmen built around 3000 BC, its capstone weighing around 10 tons. It collapsed in 1966 and was re-erected in 2014.
checker_fails.label: hair-split
checker_fails.note: the 'dolmen weighs' reading is a grammar over-parse (gold dubious)

checker_fails.name: Pigi Artemidos
checker_fails.card: Road builders at the foot of lower Olympus found Pigi Artemidos, a Bronze Age settlement: a stone-ringed tumulus holding nine tombs, and bronze knives, needles and a spiral earring.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Welsh Way
checker_fails.card: Across the Cotswold Hills ran the Welsh Way, an Iron Age trade route from South Wales to the Oxford area, later improved by the Roman army. Today it survives as a named lane.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Arroyo de Piedra
checker_fails.card: Hieroglyphs tell that Arroyo de Piedra and Tamarindito once formed an independent Maya polity. Then Dos Pilas rose, and in the 8th century the city was apparently abandoned.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: the referent of 'the city' is ambiguous

checker_fails.name: Khichuqaqa
checker_fails.card: On the slope of the mountain Kapuliyuq, about 3,160 metres up in the Cusco Region, Khichuqaqa holds rock paintings, and tombs lie nearby. Come and look at what the painters left.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: 'Come and look' is a call to action

checker_fails.name: Simanya Cave
checker_fails.card: Simanya Cave winds 372 m into the Sant Llorenç del Munt massif. Chalcolithic ceramics surfaced here in 1911, and between 1929 and 1930 Pau Codina's surveys found a large amount of pottery.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Pyramid of Sekhemkhet- Buried Pyramid
checker_fails.card: At Saqqara, a narrow passage descends about 61 m beneath the Buried Pyramid of Sekhemkhet, whose sarcophagus is cut from a single block of fine alabaster, its lid sealed with mortar.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: 61 m passage length read as a depth

checker_fails.name: Izamal
checker_fails.card: Izamal, probably the biggest city of the Northern Yucatec Plains, built in megalithic carved blocks and rounded corners, and was later a pilgrimage site rivaled only by Chichen Itza.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Limes Germanicus
checker_fails.card: At its height the Limes Germanicus ran from the Rhine's North Sea outlet to near Regensburg: bank, ditch, palisade and watchtowers between the Roman Empire and unsubdued Germanic tribes.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Eastern Gate of Philippopolis
checker_fails.card: On the main road to Byzantium stood the Eastern Gate of Philippopolis, rebuilt in the 4th century with one wide central entrance, two narrower side entrances and two watch towers.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: the towers are tied to the rebuild

checker_fails.name: Balanica
checker_fails.card: In the Sićevo Gorge, the Balanica caves yielded half a hominin jaw in 2006, lying 1.5 m below the artifact-bearing level: the first such find from controlled digs in the Central Balkans.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: 'with firm stratigraphic context' dropped from a 'first' claim

checker_fails.name: Odeon of Philippopolis
checker_fails.card: In a corner of Plovdiv's Roman forum lies the Odeon of Philippopolis, a council house that doubled as a theatre, with a Corinthian skene two stories high above orchestra and cavea.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Spy Cave
checker_fails.card: In 1886 Spy Cave yielded Neanderthal fossils of excellent quality. Its small chambers also held almost 12,000 Pleistocene remains of mammoth, cave hyena, woolly rhinoceros and cave bear.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: a partial species list presented as the full list; an invented find spot

checker_fails.name: Uragh Stone Circle
checker_fails.card: Between Lough Inchiquin and Lough Cloonee Upper, the Bronze Age Uragh Stone Circle sets five low megaliths beside a standing stone ten feet high, its centre dug out by treasure seekers.
checker_fails.label: hair-split
checker_fails.note: the 'largest standing stone' is the one large stone (gold dubious)

checker_fails.name: Temple of Hercules Gaditanus
checker_fails.card: Outside Gadir-Gades, perhaps as early as the 8th century BC, the Temple of Hercules Gaditanus honoured Melqart and then Hercules. Hannibal, Scipio Africanus and Caesar paid respect here.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Castro of Vieito
checker_fails.card: On the Lima River estuary, the Castro of Vieito lasted a century: a modest walled settlement of paved floors and a circular great house, where Roman coins of silver and bronze were found.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Sexi - Phoenician Colony
checker_fails.card: On the Mediterranean coast at Almuñécar lay Sexi, a Phoenician colony. Its coins of the 3rd-2nd centuries BC show the god Melqart on one face and one or two fish on the other.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Santuário Rupestre de Panóias
checker_fails.card: At the entrance of the Santuário Rupestre de Panóias, a rock bears inscriptions in Latin and Greek describing the ritual once held here, among three large rocks cut with cavities and stairs.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Kriemhildenstuhl
checker_fails.card: On the Kästenberg northwest of Bad Dürkheim, the Kriemhildenstuhl was quarried by working parties called Arbeitsköpfe, each 25 metres above the next. Excavators first came in 1884.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: NOT IN THE DIAGNOSIS'S LISTS - labelled by the builder (Claude Sonnet 5.5), the orchestrator confirms: S4 says 'individual' Arbeitskopfe stood 25 m above the next level, the card says 'each' (a quantifier widened); 'first came in 1884' is an inference from a list

checker_fails.name: Ancient City of Blanda
checker_fails.card: In the 4th century BC Lucanians rebuilt the village on the Palècastro hill and ringed it with a city wall. The Ancient City of Blanda left a necropolis and a large quantity of ceramics.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Gazma Cave
checker_fails.card: At 1450 m above sea level, Gazma Cave was a Paleolithic dwelling site: its 6 cultural layers yielded fauna fossils and 874 stone tools, in forms like those from Azokh and Tağlar caves.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Nesebar
checker_fails.card: Known as the Pearl of the Black Sea, the ancient part of Nesebar sits on a peninsula beyond a narrow human-made isthmus, with remains of an acropolis, a temple of Apollo and an agora.
checker_fails.label: hair-split
checker_fails.note: the location of the remains (gold dubious or over-strict)

checker_fails.name: Shipton Hill Settlement
checker_fails.card: Inside the oval enclosure of Shipton Hill Settlement, a rare Iron Age defended settlement in Dorset, digs found pottery sherds, hammer stones, flint flakes, scrapers and bits of quern-stone.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Temple of Ptah, Sekhmet and Nefertom
checker_fails.card: At Karnak, six small gateways built close together lead into the central sanctuary of the Temple of Ptah, where his statue stands. Excavators found baboon figurines and stelae with his name.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Temple of Augustus, Split
checker_fails.card: Bronze letters nailed to its stones once spelled out the dedication of the Temple of Augustus. Made a church under Byzantine rule, it survived to modern times, later serving as a granary.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: namesake: the description is about Pula; both models fail it again

checker_fails.name: Salzofen Cave
checker_fails.card: In 1924 two hunters sheltering from a storm in Salzofen Cave found fossilized bones at its entrance. The next day a school principal began to dig, unearthing large amounts of bone fossils.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: 'the next day' anchored to the wrong event

checker_fails.name: Roman Thermae, Varna
checker_fails.card: In Varna, once Odessus, stand the Roman Thermae, the largest in the Balkans, with frigidarium, tepidarium, caldarium and palaestra, heated by an underfloor hypocaust.
checker_fails.label: wrong
checker_fails.note: S3 literally contains 'the largest in the Balkans'

checker_fails.name: Temple of Augustus, Split
checker_fails.card: Bronze letters nailed to the architrave once spelled out the dedication of the Temple of Augustus. Its Corinthian columns still stand: under Byzantine rule it became a church and survived.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: namesake: the description is about Pula; both models fail it again

checker_fails.name: Domica Cave
checker_fails.card: Among the dense speleothems of Domica Cave, post holes of dwellings and fireplaces were found in several places, traces of a human presence that reaches back to the Paleolithic.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: the post holes are tied to the Paleolithic

checker_fails.name: Machu Pitumarka
checker_fails.card: On a hill northeast of Pitumarka, at the southern shore of the river Ch'illkamayu, the ruined walls of Machu Pitumarka keep watch over the Cusco Region. Climb up and see what still stands.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: Pyramid G1-d
checker_fails.card: In 1992, work to remove a road on the Giza plateau uncovered Pyramid G1-d, a satellite in the complex of Khufu with a height of 13.8 metres and a slope very similar to the Great Pyramid's.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: the original height is presented as the current height

checker_fails.name: Lohra Megalithic Tomb
checker_fails.card: In 1931 a farmer ploughing near Marburg hit an obstacle: the Lohra Megalithic Tomb, where 20 vessels placed on the chamber floor lay beneath human ashes, almost fully preserved.
checker_fails.label: wrong
checker_fails.note: S8 states all four 'unsupported' claims; the recorded checker missed S8

checker_fails.name: Stoke Hill
checker_fails.card: North of Exeter rises Stoke Hill, crowned at 159 metres by a Roman signal station. Just below lies an Iron Age hill fort, with sight of a number of other hill forts at once.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: 'better position to have sight' becomes 'with sight'

checker_fails.name: Tal-Barrani
checker_fails.card: In Tal-Barrani, a milk depot's builders uncovered three Punic rock-cut tombs; in May 1993, trenching along the road revealed a multi-chambered catacomb and a Late Roman chamber tomb.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Samothrace Temple Complex
checker_fails.card: On three narrow terraces of mount Hagios Georgios, between two steep-banked torrents, the Samothrace Temple Complex was celebrated throughout Ancient Greece for its Mystery religion.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: the torrents separate the terraces; the card puts the whole complex between them

checker_fails.name: Caves of Poço Velho
checker_fails.card: In the centre of Cascais, the Caves of Poço Velho held a necropolis of around 115 burials, with limestone votive offerings such as cylindrical idols and decorated schist slabs.
checker_fails.label: substantive
checker_fails.note: NOT IN THE DIAGNOSIS'S LISTS - labelled by the builder (Claude Sonnet 5.5), the orchestrator confirms: 'evidence points to their use as a necropolis' became 'held a necropolis' (a sharpened hedge); the schist slabs are made an example of limestone votive offerings

checker_fails.name: Knossos
checker_fails.card: On Kephala hill in the Kairatos valley, Knossos was settled about 7000 BC; its first palace rose around 1900 BC, and the Palace of Minos still dominates the site.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Piruro
checker_fails.card: Above the river Tantamayo, over 3.8 km above sea level, the Fortress of Piruro II rises five stories, its walls built with stones hewn in squared shape and uniform size.
checker_fails.label: substantive

checker_fails.name: La Grotte des Fées
checker_fails.card: Railway builders near Châtelperron first found La Grotte des Fées around 1840, perhaps in 1848. Within lay several thousand flint blades and mammoth tusks of over 2 metres long.
checker_fails.label: hair-split

checker_fails.name: Ta' Kaċċatura
checker_fails.card: On a long, flat ridge between Wied Dalam and Wied Żembaq, Ta' Kaċċatura holds a rustic Roman villa and underground cisterns, witness to a thriving olive oil industry.
checker_fails.label: hair-split
